summary: Mt. Hood NF lookout in the Bull Run Watershed: 1906 camp, 1933 tower, 41-foot L-4 cab built 1952-54; staffed under a Portland Water Bureau agreement since 2007; escort-only access.

facts.design: 41-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab

access.note: Official escort only per NHLR; firelookout.com says closed to public entry; Cheryl Hill directory lists it as not accessible to the public. Site is in the Bull Run Watershed.

corrections.why: 2.1 m is not supported by any source read. The Register describes a 41-foot timber tower and firelookout.com gives 41 feet for the present tower; 41 ft is about 12.5 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register dates the L-4 to 1952, firelookout.com to a 1953 replacement, the history page to a 1954 replacement, and Portland's water bureau to the early 1950s. The story gives all of these and does not pick one.
The Register gives 4,161 ft (1,268 m), matching the record. firelookout.com gives 4385 ft and the Cheryl Hill directory gives 4,835 ft. The record is kept at the Register figure for editor review.

The Register and history page say 41 feet; the water bureau says the lookout stands 45 feet above the butte; a 1953 survey note on the history page says approximately 50 feet. Height_m is set from the 41-foot figure.

firelookout.com says staffed with volunteers, while the 2022 water bureau article says volunteers were replaced by a contract arrangement in 2007. The story follows the newer, more detailed bureau account.
The Register says ground quarters were added later; firelookout.com says the ground L-4 living quarters were built in 1933. Timing is reported as disputed.

notes_for_editor: Construction dates for the present tower differ across four sources (1952, 1953, 1954, early 1950s); the story reports the disagreement. The Water Bureau's 2022 article names the contractor; the story leaves the name out. Water Bureau article gives a 2022 renewal request with no outcome found. Mt. Hood NF Facebook post (Oct 17, 2022) says staffed each summer since built; not used. Trail Advocates archive and a 2022 Portland council impact statement were surfaced by search but not read. No photos added. Height_m 12.5 is a unit conversion of the 41-foot figure.
